messages:
sarah_support: heads-up — escalated from CS. ACME (ticket ACME-12345) seeing intermittent SSE stream cutoffs mid-response and occasional 401s on long streams. Need a reproducible cURL and request IDs to pull debug bundle.

miguel_eng: can you paste a couple request IDs + exact timestamps? also which endpoint & model?

sarah_support: from logs:
request_id=01GTZ5A2JQ0B4E7YF6Z0X1A 2026-11-03T14:12:07Z
request_id=01GTZ5A2JQ0B4E7YF6Z0X1B 2026-11-03T14:15:33Z
endpoint: POST /v1/streams/generate (https://api.redwood.ai)
model: redwood-open-7b
symptoms: stream cuts off after ~10–20s, sometimes followed by a 401 in headers.

alyssa_cs: customer can run curl — want minimal repro they can run locally. their tokens are short-lived via SDK; could be rotation.

miguel_eng: here's a minimal repro to ask them to run (replace token):

```bash
curl -v -N -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Client-Version: acme-1.2.3" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-7b","input":"stream test","max_tokens":500}' \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate" --max-time 120
```

miguel_eng: ask them to paste the full HTTP response (headers + body), and specifically the X-Request-Id / x-request-id header values and any 401 WWW-Authenticate header if present.

ryan_oncall: if they can reproduce, run our support collector. ingest-bot command below (internal):

ingest-bot: to collect server-side traces run:

```bash
supportctl collect --request-id 01GTZ5A2JQ0B4E7YF6Z0X1A --ticket ACME-12345 --include-logs --output acme-01.zip
```

ingest-bot: attach acme-01.zip here or upload to the ticket. If 401 occurs, include the full Authorization header (redact token) and the token issue timestamp.

sarah_support: i've pinged the customer with the curl + collection steps. asked for x-request-id and raw --include output. will update when they reply :eyes:

miguel_eng: on my side i'll grep auth middleware + gateway flush logs for those request ids and time window. also look for proxy timeouts or buffer limits.

sarah_support: thanks — keeping this thread open.
